page_title: Keyameleon: Switch Keyboard Layout per Keyboard on Mac

sources.entry: Keyameleon - Open-source tool that gives each physical keyboard its own input source and switches to it automatically as you type. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/mastro993/keyameleon) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: Keyameleon
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source Mac menu bar app that assigns each physical keyboard its own input source and switches to it automatically as you type.
use_cases: Typing in English on a built-in keyboard and Italian on an external keyboard at the same time
Using a Japanese Kana input method on one keyboard and a U.S. layout on another
Avoiding manual input source switching when changing keyboards
Keeping different layouts per physical keyboard across apps and websites
summary.what_it_does: Keyameleon lets you choose an input source (such as U.S., Italian, Dvorak, or Japanese Kana) for each keyboard you use. When a key press comes from a keyboard, it detects which device it came from and switches to that keyboard's assigned input source. It recognizes the MacBook's built-in keyboard and external keyboards, remembers them across disconnects and restarts, and lets you rename or hide devices that are not keyboards. The page states it only observes keyboard activity to identify the source device and does not log or send what you type.
notable: Switches input source per physical keyboard rather than per app or window
Open source under MIT license; source code available for inspection
Installable via Homebrew cask or DMG from GitHub releases
caveats: Requires Input Monitoring permission during setup
Switches after the key press, so the first key or keys typed during the switch may use the previous input source
